newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes pile up at Paris airports, delays seen.
newsitem.headline: Strikes pile up at Paris airports, delays seen.

text.p: Unions at Paris airports called a 24-hour strike for Tuesday, adding to stoppages at Air France Europe, but airlines expected the protests would at the worst cause slight delays.
Spokeswomen for Air France and subsidiary Air France Europe said on Monday both state-owned airlines maintained all their scheduled flights.
The Air France spokeswoman said all airlines operating from Paris' Charles de Gaulle and Orly airport could suffer slight delays because of slower luggage handling.
Airport staff are protesting against planned job cuts.

Ground staff at Air France Europe vowed to join a 48-hour strike by some of the airline's pilots over the unifying of their pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France in a merger between the two airlines becoming effective on Tuesday.

Air France Europe said the pilots' protest failed to disrupt flights on Monday, the end of a busy extended Easter holiday weekend. Pilots' unions said one third of flights were cancelled and they expected more disruption on Tuesday.

Junior Transport Minister Anne-Marie Idrac told France-Inter radio she was apalled by the repeated strikes, saying they jeopardised the state airlines' future as French airspace opens up to competition from Tuesday under European open skies rules.
Ground staff strikes forced Air France Europe to cancel many flights on Saturday and all flights on Sunday.
